$comment: The claims ladder of proofs/README.md, declared as DATA so a registry can read it rather
than parse prose. Hand-authored and never generated: the point of the manifest is that a
human decided which rung each claim sits on, and a generator would only be able to restate
`level` is a CLOSED set — proved | tested | assumed | policy — and the four map onto the
README's four rungs: proved, differentially tested, assumed-and-stated, and not-claimed.
A `policy` entry is an exclusion carrying its reason, because an unstated exclusion reads,
to whoever finds it later, as a claim that failed.
A `proved` entry names ONE theorem, its model and the prover pin, so an evidence check can
resolve the theorem in the named model and the pin in the named file. Nothing here is checkable by
reading this file alone, and that is the intended shape: the manifest says where to look,
the proof leg (proofs/check.ps1) is what looks.
Every later proof phase in this repository appends its claims here rather than starting a
The schema is Fuaran-Core's proofs/kit/LADDER.md: `claim`, and evidence {theorem, model,
prover, supporting} | {family, cases, host, model, artifact, seeds} | {assumption} | {document} by
level. A lemma a theorem leans on is listed under `supporting` and checked like the theorem; one
that is a claim in its own right gets its own row. Other keys (mitigation, reason, note) are commentary.
subject: Fuaran-Program
$scope: the proved models under proofs/: the shared bounded fold — BoundedActions.runBoundedActionWith, the one interpreter every placement runs, over the closed Action union, its State store, its closure-free client effects and its diagnostics (Phase 1715), restated over the generic tier's ActionView and the fold-read members of the ProgramWitness contract (DECISIONS.md D18) and re-proved there before the generic core is written, with the fourteen-arm union kept as the UI witness seen through the view (Phase 1898); and the interaction budget — Budget.satAdd/satMul, Budget.actionCascadeCost, Budget.treeCost and the G2 stage of BoundedDriver.step that refuses on them (Phase 1716); and two-phase staging — Handler.run's plan phase, phase boundary and perform phase with the performer abstract, DECISIONS.md D8's law that the residual of a failed handler is exactly the prefix of staged host calls that ran (Phase 1717). and the effect gate — ServerEffectRegistry.Gate consulted before any performer, the policy an operator declares over the trace of performed effects, and the return contract ServerEffectRegistry.registerChecked composes with a performer, proved over the staging model with the performer abstract (Phase 1759). Bounded code and bounded cost, the two halves of running an untrusted generated tree on shared infrastructure; bounded residue, what a handler that reaches outside can leave behind; and a constrained boundary, what reaches a performer and what it can hand back.

claims.claim: The fold is defined on every arm of the closed Action union — no wildcard, no partial match, no throw — and one step that is neither the composition arm nor a call the placement answered is characterised structurally: the placement accumulation is untouched, the store is either unchanged or written at exactly one key the host-reserved predicate rejects, and at most one client effect and at most one diagnostic are emitted.

evidence.note: since Phase 1898 a corollary of `fold_total` at the UI witness: `run` is the generic fold applied to `ui_view`, and `ui_view` names every constructor with no wildcard exactly as `handled` does, so a fifteenth arm fails to compile in the adapter's View exactly as it fails in the fold — the exhaustiveness check D18 moves into the adapter, checked here by the same means

claims.claim: The generic fold is defined on every shape of the action view — Sequence, Assign, Call, Leaf — with no wildcard, no partial match and no throw, for every witness; and one step that is neither Sequence nor a call the placement answered is characterised structurally: the placement accumulation is untouched, the store is either unchanged or written at exactly one key the witness's reserved predicate rejects, and at most one effect and at most one diagnostic are emitted. For a leaf that is the kept assumption K3 made a theorem: whatever the witness's Lower answers, this is the most it can do.

evidence.note: unconditional. Termination is structural on the view, carried by the decreases clause on `fold`/`fold_many`; the view is taken to exhaustion (a tree), so the obligation that a witness's View unfolds finitely is carried by the TYPE of the witness's `w_view` field — a Tot arrow — rather than by a fuel; `ui_view` discharges it for the UI witness by being accepted as Tot

claims.claim: Two actions differing ONLY in the closures they carry produce identical outcomes and identical placement accumulations. A fold that invoked a carried closure could not satisfy this, so the safety property the interpreter's own header states — a generated tree running through this fold has no arbitrary-code-execution surface — is a theorem rather than a comment.

evidence.note: since Phase 1898 this is `run_action_blind` — the generic theorem, conditional on the witness obligation `blind_to` — at the UI witness, with `ui_blind_to_closures` discharging that obligation under `same_but_closures`; so the UI statement is unconditional again. The closure slots have an abstract type parameter with no elimination form, so in the model a fold that DID invoke one cannot be written at all; the lemma is what makes that absence a statement rather than an accident of how the model was written

claims.claim: The core's half of no-closure-invocation, held unconditionally: two views of the same shape — the same constructors at every node, the same keys, values, expressions, endpoints and target flags, the carried actions describing alike and, at a leaf, lowering alike at every node id and store — fold to identical outcomes and identical placements, for every witness and every arm. The generic fold reads an action only through the witness's Describe and Lower and the shape its View gave it, so it cannot have applied anything the witness did not surface.

evidence.note: unconditional. This is the half D18 keeps in the core: the view carries no closure and the action type parameter has no elimination form, so there is nothing for the fold to invoke

claims.claim: No-closure-invocation for the generic core, CONDITIONAL on the witness: under any relation on actions the witness is blind to — its View sends related actions to same-shaped views — related actions run to identical outcomes and placements. This is the obligation D18 places on the witness (only a View or a Lower could reach a closure), stated as a precondition; the UI witness discharges it (ui-witness-blind-to-closures) and any other domain inherits it as its own.
claims.conditional_on: blind_to rel w — the witness's View sends rel-related actions to same-shaped views (same_shape); the differential test through a test witness (Phase 1896) is the sampled form of this for a domain that does not prove it

claims.claim: The UI witness meets the no-closure obligation: under same_but_closures — two actions differing only in the closures they carry — ui_view produces same-shaped views. Describe and Lower read the constructor, the route, the payload, the encoding and the node id, never a closure slot; composition needs one induction. This is what makes run_no_closure unconditional at the UI witness rather than a conditional nobody has met.

Running the concatenation of two operation lists equals running the first and then the second against the store the first left, with the effect lists and the diagnostic lists concatenated in order and the placement threaded through. This is DECISIONS.md D7's splice property — a nested call sees the writes before it and is seen by the writes after it — stated as an equation.

evidence.note: since Phase 1898 the action-level statement (Phase 1715's `chain_action_homomorphism`, now under the headline name) — `sequence_homomorphism` at the UI witness, through `ui_view_list_app`: viewing a concatenation is concatenating the views

claims.claim: Over the view, for every witness: running the concatenation of two operation lists equals running the first and then the second against the store the first left, with the effect lists and the diagnostic lists concatenated in order and the placement threaded through. DECISIONS.md D7's splice property as an equation, now the generic tier's — what makes Sequence a composition rather than a fifth special case.

evidence.note: the store is modelled CONCRETELY as a keyed association list — D18's StoreWitness.Assign is `write` — because this theorem is about what is written, and a theorem about writes to an abstract store would be a theorem about an obligation nobody had stated; see store-keyed-channel-assumed

claims.claim: The two placements that run no handlers meet `host-reserved-keys-untouched`'s side condition: their handler arm preserves every host-reserved State key. This is what keeps that theorem from being a conditional nobody has met. Since Phase 1898 it is quantified over EVERY reserved predicate, so it discharges `view-reserved-untouched`'s condition for any domain whose placement declines every call.

Every member of the generic witness is a total arrow the model takes as a parameter, and each is an assumption the theorems lean on: View is total and, applied to exhaustion, finite (its field type is a Tot arrow onto a tree, so a View that put an action inside its own Sequence cannot be written); Lower answers a leaf outcome — at most one effect, or a refusal, or a decline, and never a store (K3, by type); Describe and Resolve are total and pure, the same answer for the same store; IsReserved is a total predicate and ReservedPrefix a constant (K5). Nothing proved depends on WHAT any of them answers.

evidence.assumption: a domain's ProgramWitness members are total arrows of the shapes the witness record declares: View unfolds every action to a finite view, Lower returns a leaf outcome, Describe and Resolve are pure, IsReserved is a predicate

claims.mitigation: the UI witness discharges every row in the model itself (ui_view is accepted as Tot, ui_lower returns leaf_outcome by type, describe and ui_resolve are pure definitions over the eight axioms), and the differential host is what says that discharged instance is the shipped one; Phase 1896's test witness carries the same obligations for the ported core

claims.claim: The store is modelled concretely as one keyed state channel — an association list where StoreWitness.Assign is `write` — rather than abstractly behind the witness (D18 s3.4), because view-reserved-untouched is a theorem about what is written. What is assumed of a domain is therefore K4: its Assign writes exactly one key of one state channel. A store whose Assign did something else is outside the model.

evidence.assumption: a domain store's Assign writes exactly one key of one keyed state channel, and lookup after Assign agrees with Map semantics (replace in place, append otherwise)

claims.mitigation: the differential host projects the domain store onto the channel (today BindingSources.State as a key-ordered list) and compares it key by key after every step, so an Assign that wrote elsewhere diverges on the first action that writes

claims.claim: The Leaf shape's LeafDeclaration — the effect kinds and host calls a leaf may demand — is OUT of the fold theorem.
claims.reason: it is the DEMANDED projection's input, read by Demanded and never by the fold; the fold does with a leaf exactly what Lower says, so a model of the fold that carried the declaration would be modelling a static projection and calling the result a property of the interpreter. The view carries the action instead, which is what Describe and Lower need.

This is the only thing that says the proved model is about the code that runs.

claims.claim: The durable journal is OUT of the theorem.
claims.reason: it is a placement concern — what a session persists between interactions and how a replay reconstructs it — and the fold is placement-neutral by construction. A model that reached into it would be modelling one placement and calling the result a property of the interpreter.

claims.claim: The browser placement's loop is OUT of the theorem.
claims.reason: the theorems are about the shared fold, which the browser placement runs unchanged; everything ABOVE it there — the transport, the effect performer, the DOM patch application — is neither modelled nor claimed. A reader should take 'the fold is total and invokes no closure' and nothing more from this about what a browser does.

claims.claim: The per-connection session cells (BoundedConnection) are OUT of the theorem.
claims.reason: same boundary as the journal. The fold takes a store and returns a store; who owns that store between interactions, and what concurrency it is subject to, is the placement's question and is not answered anywhere in proofs/.

claims.claim: The per-interaction resource budget is OUT of the bounded-fold theorem (Phase 1715).
claims.reason: bounded CODE and bounded COST are the two halves of running an untrusted tree on shared infrastructure, and only the first is proved by proofs/BoundedFold.fst. The budget is the driver's (Budget.fs). It is now proved SEPARATELY — the Phase 1716 claims below, from proofs/Budget.fst — and the two models are joined by nothing but the directory they sit in: no law of either follows from the other, and reading one as covering the other would be the more dangerous of the two mistakes.

claims.claim: The saturating add and multiply are monotone in both arguments, never answer below zero, never answer above the saturation bound, and agree with ordinary arithmetic everywhere below it. A cost is a budget comparand, so an overflow that wrapped negative would read as cheap and admit the very tree the budget exists to refuse; monotonicity is the other half of the same requirement, since a bigger tree must not price smaller.

evidence.note: the saturation bound is a PARAMETER of the model rather than Int32.MaxValue baked in, so the lemma holds for every bound and nothing proved here is an artefact of the width production happens to have; see int32-bound-assumed for what that leaves open

claims.claim: When treeCost's answer is at or below the ceiling it is the EXACT cost — equal to what the same walk with no ceiling at all would have returned. The early stop that keeps the pricing function from itself becoming unbounded work costs nothing in the case where the number is used as a number, which matters because the session records it as NodeCount and prices later events against it.

When the exact cost of a tree is above the ceiling, treeCost's answer is above the ceiling too. The early stop never turns a refusal into an admission — the only direction that matters, and the one an optimisation to a budget function could silently break.

evidence.note: the asymmetry with treecost-exact-below-ceiling is deliberate: above the ceiling the answer is only ever 'more than this', which is all a refusal needs

claims.claim: The tree walk terminates on every finite tree, and visits at most as many nodes as the tree has AND at most ceiling+1 of them. Termination is carried by the decreases clause on the walk itself — a measure over the pending stack, not a depth counter — and the second bound is the ceiling acting as fuel: a tree ten thousand times over budget costs the same as one marginally over.

evidence.note: the ceiling bound carries a side condition — the ceiling is below the saturation bound — and it is not a technicality: at InteractionBudget.unlimited the two coincide, the accumulator saturates at a value the guard still admits, and walking the whole tree is the intended behaviour rather than a bound anyone wanted

claims.claim: A step the budget refuses returns the session it was given — not an equal one, the same one — with no patches, no effects, and a named refusal carrying its reason. Never an exception: the model has no exceptions, so the Tot effect on the modelled step is what makes production's total signature a thing the prover checks rather than a convention a reader must notice.

evidence.note: quantified over EVERY admitted branch, which is what makes it a statement about the gate rather than about one driver: whatever the driver would have done to the session had the budget admitted the event, a breach does none of it

claims.claim: The extracted budget model and the shipped pricing functions return the SAME INTEGER for the trees the bounded driver's own suite drives and for generated trees — fans, chains, every data-bearing kind, a payload at the counting cap, a payload past it, and a chart whose multiply saturates — each priced at every ceiling around its own exact cost; the same for the action cascade cost; and the model's gate agrees with BoundedDriver.step's G2 stage on the verdict, on the refusal's reason verbatim, and on the session coming back by reference.

The comparison is of the INTEGER and not the verdict, which is what says the model kept production's explicit stack in production's push order — above the ceiling the answer depends on which nodes were visited first. The go-red case commits a walk that accumulates with .NET's wrapping add and asserts BOTH that the harness reports it and that its ceiling comparison comes out the wrong way, the tree being admitted rather than refused; a divergence that was merely a different number would not demonstrate the defect the law excludes

claims.claim: The counted rows of a data-bearing node's Binding.Static payload are modelled as a LIST with a counting cap. Production's payload is a seq, which may be lazy and may be unbounded, and Seq.truncate is what bounds the reading of it. So what is proved is that the cap is applied and that the cost it produces is bounded by it — never that a seq is finite, and never that reading one terminates.

evidence.assumption: a Binding.Static payload read through Seq.truncate behaves as the capped list the model counts

claims.mitigation: the differential host's corpus includes a payload AT the cap and one PAST it, and reads the cap out of the extraction rather than restating production's private literal, so a divergence between the two is reported rather than papered over

claims.claim: The model is over unbounded integers; production is over Int32, with the ceiling's upper limit at Int32.MaxValue. The two coincide on every input production can be handed — an int64 sum and an int64 product of two Int32s both fit with room to spare, which is exactly what production computes before narrowing — so the model is over a WIDER domain than production rather than a different one. Budget.actionCascadeCost is the one function with no saturation at all, in the model or in production: what bounds it there is the Int32 range, and that is this rung rather than the proved one.

evidence.assumption: the model's unbounded integers agree with production's Int32 arithmetic on every input production can be handed

claims.mitigation: the saturation bound is a parameter, so every proved law is quantified over it and holds at Int32.MaxValue as a special case; the differential supplies Int32.MaxValue and includes a tree whose cost saturates and one whose node cost saturates inside the multiply

claims.claim: Which NodeKind is data-bearing, and which of its fields carries the rows and the weights, is supplied to the model by the differential host as a cost shape. NodeKind has scores of arms and Budget.nodeCost reads four of them; a model that carried the union would be modelling the tree vocabulary rather than the budget. The consequence, stated plainly: a production change that began weighting a fifth kind would be invisible to the differential until the host's projection gained the kind too.

evidence.assumption: the cost shape the differential host supplies names every NodeKind Budget.nodeCost weights, and the fields it reads

claims.mitigation: the line is drawn where a defect is silent rather than loud — a mis-weighted kind prices visibly wrong on the first tree that contains one, where a wrapping add prices wrong only on the trees nobody tries; and the differential's corpus exercises all four kinds the projection names, so a projection that stopped matching one is caught

claims.claim: That MaxActions and MaxNodes are the RIGHT numbers is OUT of the theorem.
claims.reason: they are policy, set by the host per placement. Everything proved here says a tree is priced correctly against whatever number is set and refused when it exceeds it; nothing says a number is well chosen, and a proof could not.

claims.claim: Wall-clock cost is OUT of the theorem.
claims.reason: the budget is step- and size-based on purpose — no Stopwatch, no Date.now — so that the same tree and event sequence bound identically at every placement and are unit-testable headlessly. It bounds WORK, not time. A tree within budget can still be slow on a slow machine, and reading these laws as a latency guarantee would be reading them as something they were deliberately not built to be.

claims.claim: Nothing external runs in the plan phase. The plan phase's output — the store, the staged list, the audit trail, the patches, the notifications, the client effects and the diagnostics — is a function of the entry state, the program, the witness and the registry's gate, argument policy and performer lookup ALONE: under every behaviour the performers could have, it is EQUAL. And the record of what ran outside is untouched by planning.

evidence.note: statable because the model splits production's HostFunctions map — name to closure — into a LOOKUP (name to an opaque performer token, read while planning) and a BEHAVIOUR (token and argument to a result, read only while performing); the theorem replaces the behaviour by an arbitrary other and shows the plan equal. In the differential host the token is production's own closure and the behaviour is application, so the split loses nothing

claims.claim: When the plan completed and the performer fails at position k of the staged list — any list, any position — the outcome's store is the ENTRY store, the handler is uncommitted, it carries no patches, no notifications and no client effects, and Performed is EXACTLY the first k staged capabilities, in declaration order. Not at most a prefix: the prefix, and which one.

evidence.note: plan_halt_performs_nothing is the plan-phase half of the same clause: a handler that halted while planning reports nothing performed, under every performer at once, because nothing reached the perform phase

claims.claim: For EVERY performer: when the plan completed, the handler commits exactly when every staged call ran, and Performed is the plan phase's capabilities in stage order (on commit; nothing on rollback) followed by the staged capabilities the performer answered, in DECLARATION order — the first `ran` of them, where `ran` counts the calls answered before the first refusal. Execution order, as an equation, and the general form the prefix and total-prefix corollaries read off.

evidence.note: perform_spec is the inductive core — the whole behaviour of the perform phase stated once: it halts exactly when the performer refused before the end of the list, records as run the prefix it answered in declaration order appended to what was recorded before, and touches nothing else the outcome reads

claims.claim: When every staged call succeeds the handler commits, and Performed is the plan phase's capabilities in stage order followed by the WHOLE staged list in declaration order — the residual, on success, is everything.

The extracted staging model and Handler.run produce the SAME outcome — canonical tree, state, query slots, verdict, audit trail, patches, notifications, client effects and diagnostics — over the HandlerLoopTests and DurableInterpreterTests staging cases and every plan-phase halt, each run with a scripted performer that refuses at every position of the staged list and once not at all; the two performers are asked the same calls in the same order; and production's Performed is the performer's own log of what ran.

claims.claim: What production does WITH a query, an op, a landing slot, a Compute stage, the gate and the argument policy reaches the model as arrows — LandQuery, Assign, IsReserved, ReservedPrefix, the op stream's Apply, runInert, the query evaluator reduced to a halt-or-land, Gate, and ServerArgumentPolicy.check with its defect described — and each is supplied to the model from production's own member. The theorems are quantified over every witness and every registry; the differential is over the extraction of everything else.

evidence.assumption: the differential host's translation supplies each arrow from the production member the model names for it

claims.mitigation: the differential exercises every arm each arrow feeds — a query that lands and one that fails, an op that applies and one that is refused, a slot that lands and a reserved one, a Compute stage that writes, a gate that refuses, a policy that refuses, a lookup that misses — and the diagnostics are compared verbatim, so an arrow wired to the wrong member diverges on the first case that reaches it

claims.claim: The indeterminate window D12 declares — a step journaled as attempted and never decided — is OUT of the theorem, as the durable journal itself is (the `durable-journal` entry above).
claims.reason: the theorem says what Performed reports when the performer ANSWERS, and nothing about a performer that never does; the durable interpreter CALLS Handler.run and does not fork it, so it sits above the model. The window is declared rather than closed by D12 on its own argument — the effect commits in a system this host does not own — and no proof here narrows it. Stated rather than left absent, because an unstated exclusion reads, to whoever finds it later, as a claim that failed.

claims.claim: What a host function DOES when invoked is OUT of the theorem.
claims.reason: it is the host's. The theorem bounds what the handler reports and when it stops asking; it cannot bound what an invocation did, and the go-red case exists to show that a performer's report and its act are two different things the differential must check against each other.

claims.claim: A capability the gate refuses reaches no performer and lands exactly one denial carrying the capability and never the payload. The planned accumulator is halted, its diagnostics are the one GateRefused denial over what was there, every other field is the entry field, and the result is EQUAL under every performer lookup, every performer behaviour, every argument policy and every witness — none is read before the gate has answered.
